reasoning_trace.value: The paper includes several figures and diagrams, including Fig. 1, which illustrates the concept of signal-signal beat interference (SSBI) in a self-coherent system. Fig. 2 shows the principle of the proposed photonics-aided THz ISAC system, including the architecture and spectra at key points. Fig. 3 depicts the complex trajectory of the integrated signal, and Fig. 4 displays the spectra and zero-Doppler cuts of ambiguity functions of the OFDM signal and its SSBI signal. Fig. 5 illustrates the 3-dB resolution of the OFDM and its SSBI under different bandwidths. Fig. 6 shows the real signals in the time domain, including the OFDM, its SSBI, and their dot product. Fig. 7 presents the heterogeneous diversity filtering process and its enhancements in sensing performance metrics. Fig. 8 shows the experimental setup of the proposed THz ISAC system. Fig. 9 is a photograph of the experimental platform. Fig. 10 displays the spectrum of the ISAC waveform before the AWG and the PAPR reduction of the integrated signal. Fig. 11 shows the optical spectrum before the THz PD and the electrical spectrum after the THz ED. Fig. 12 presents the BER versus CSPR with/without using the KK algorithm. Fig. 13 compares the PAPR under two different transmission schemes. Fig. 14 displays the output SNRs of different filters, and Fig. 15 shows the PSLR and 3-dB resolution of the matched filter and the nonlinear matched filter under different transmitted CSPRs.

reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The proposed system is a photonics-aided THz ISAC system using a self-coherent OFDM scheme. The system mechanism involves the use of a virtual carrier to enhance the sensing performance. The ISAC coupling mode is based on the signal-signal beat interference (SSBI), which is typically considered destructive but is transformed into a constructive component using a nonlinear matched filtering (NMF) approach. The NMF enables the extraction of sensing information from the SSBI, improving the sensing metrics such as resolution and peak-sidelobe ratio (PSLR).

reasoning_trace.description: Validate the physical consistency of reported metrics (Rate/Resolution).
reasoning_trace.value: The paper reports a 20-Gb/s communication rate and a 1.94-cm ranging resolution. The 3-dB resolution is improved by up to 25%, and the PSLR is increased by up to 8 dB for the sensing function. The peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) of the integrated signal is reduced by up to 7 dB. These metrics are physically consistent with the system design and the experimental setup.

reasoning_trace.description: Identify the solved problems and remaining open challenges.
reasoning_trace.value: The proposed system solves the problem of improving sensing performance in THz ISAC systems by transforming SSBI into a constructive component. The system also addresses the issue of high PAPR in OFDM signals by using a virtual carrier and the RCF algorithm. However, the paper notes that the optimal CSPR for the integrated signal is higher than the PAPR of the information-bearing signal, and the system requires a careful balance between the CSPR and the PAPR to achieve optimal performance. Remaining open challenges include further improving the sensing resolution and PSLR, and exploring the use of other waveforms and signal processing techniques to enhance the system performance.
